svg.title: Four kinds of neurons side by side. Unipolar: one myelinated process leaving the cell body and branching at its end. Bipolar: dendrites at one end, the cell body in the middle of a myelinated process, and a sensory receptor at the other end. Pseudounipolar: the cell body off to the side on a short stalk joined to one long process whose lower end branches into sensory receptor endings. Multipolar: many dendrites around the cell body and a single myelinated axon.
